title: Pairs

steps.say: Notes are filled in again. This time, look for two cells that work as a team.
Two cells in this row have only 2 and 6. Tap both.
steps.nudge: Find the two cells whose notes are just 2 and 6.

steps.say: One is 2, the other is 6. Turn Pencil on.
steps.nudge: Pencil is the key at the bottom right.

steps.say: So no other cell in their row or box can be 2 or 6. Rub out those 2s.
steps.nudge: Select an outlined cell, then press 2.

steps.say: When two cells in a row, column or box share the same two notes, those numbers are taken. That's a naked pair.
Now this column: 2 and 6 fit only in these two cells. Tap both.
steps.nudge: Find the two cells in the column that still have a 2 or a 6.

steps.say: So those two cells are 2 and 6. Rub out the other note.
steps.nudge: Select the outlined cell, then press 3.

steps.say: When two numbers fit only in the same two cells, those cells keep just those two. That's a hidden pair.
Your turn: two cells in this box share the same two notes. Clear those numbers from the rest.
steps.nudge: Find two cells whose notes are the same pair. Which other cell has one of them?

steps.say: Turn Pencil off. Time to place.
steps.nudge: Tap Pencil to go back to writing answers.

steps.say: This row's 3 has only one spot left now. Place it.
steps.nudge: Which cell in the row still has a 3 note?

steps.say: Finish the board! Start with cells that have one note.
steps.nudge: Look for a cell with a single note, or a number with one spot.

outro: Solved! When two cells own the same two numbers, clear those numbers from everywhere else they reach.
